 UPDATED: F1 Mexico City Grid 2026: The Full Starting Order At The Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 
 UPDATED: F1 Mexico City grid 2026: The full starting order at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez
 Henry Valantine 
 01 Nov 2026 5:17 PM 
 Will Kimi Antonelli become World Champion in Mexico City? 
 The F1 starting grid has been set for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, with three grid penalties already announced prior to the session. 
 Lewis Hamilton took his first pole position for Ferrari in extremely competitive circumstances, pipping George Russell to pole by just 0.009s as he lines up alongside his former Mercedes teammate.
 F1 Mexico grid: The provisional 2026 starting order in Mexico City
 1. Lewis Hamilton  Ferrari 1:16.514
2. George Russell Mercedes 1:16.523
3. Charles Leclerc Ferrari 1:16.633
4. Kimi Antonelli Mercedes 1:16.707
5. Max Verstappen Red Bull [grid penalty]
6. Lando Norris McLaren 1:16.824
7. Isack Hadjar Red Bull 1:16.900
8. Arvid Lindblad Racing Bulls 1:17.117
9. Pierre Gasly Alpine 1:17.153
10. Nico Hulkenberg Audi 1:17.306
11. Franco Colapinto Alpine 1:17.640
12. Oscar Piastri McLaren 1:17.646
13. Gabriel Bortoleto Audi 1:17.680
14. Oliver Bearman Haas 1:17.847
15. Carlos Sainz Williams 1:18.885 [Q2]
16. Alex Albon Williams 1:18.630
17. Fernando Alonso Aston Martin 1:18.908
18. Ryo Hirakawa Haas 1:18.958
19. Lance Stroll Aston Martin 1:19.072
20. Sergio Perez Cadillac 1:19.105
21. Valtteri Bottas Cadillac [grid penalty]
Pit lane: Liam Lawson Racing Bulls [grid penalty]
 More about the Mexico City Grand Prix
 How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 2026 title at the Mexico City GP 
 F1 2027 driver line-up: Which drivers are already confirmed for the 2027 grid? 
 How did qualifying unfold in Mexico City?
 Both Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson knew they would be heading into the session with a one-place grid penalty each after their unusual scuffle during FP2 on Friday, while Valtteri Bottas will take a 50-place drop after taking most of a new power unit beyond his allocation.
 There was a shock Q2 exit for Oscar Piastri at McLaren, despite his strong practice showing, after Fernando Alonso had to pull over in Q1 for a suspected ERS issue at Aston Martin.
 The drivers were tightly-packed heading into Q3, with no guarantee as to who would take pole.
 Provisional pole changed hands several times, but it was Lewis Hamilton who took his first pole for three years by piecing a lap together to pip Russell to pole position.
 Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli will line up on the second row, with Max Verstappen rounding out the top five once his one-place grid penalty takes effect.
